title: PremiseCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of Human and AI Peer Reviews
abstract: arXiv:2610.21046v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Peer review is under strain from the growth of submissions, and review comments written by humans or AI can misstate what a paper says. We introduce ReviewFact, a benchmark that labels such factual errors in review comments under one definition across NLP, machine learning, and the natural sciences, and that measures cost and latency alongside accuracy. A frontier LLM checks comments well but must read the whole paper for each check, while cheap decision models, which score whether a statement holds in a text, fall far short on whole comments that mix several implicit assertions. PremiseCheck is a framework that combines the two. An LLM rewrites each comment as explicit premises without reading the paper, and a decision model checks each premise against the paper. When each comment is checked on its own, PremiseCheck reaches accuracy comparable to GPT-5.5 across all three fields at about half its cost, and on NLP reviews at a quarter o

translated_title: PremiseCheck：面向人类与AI同行评审的高效事实核查
translated_abstract: 同行评审正因投稿量的增长而承受巨大压力，无论是人类还是AI撰写的评审意见都可能错误地陈述论文的实际内容。我们提出了ReviewFact，这是一个在统一定义下对NLP、机器学习和自然科学领域评审意见中的事实性错误进行标注的基准，并同时衡量准确率、成本和延迟。前沿大语言模型能够很好地检查评审意见，但每次检查都必须通读整篇论文；而廉价的判定模型（用于判断某陈述在文本中是否成立）在处理混合了多个隐含断言的完整评审意见时表现远为逊色。PremiseCheck是一个将两者结合的框架：由一个LLM在不阅读论文的情况下将每条评审意见改写为显式前提，再由判定模型将每个前提与论文逐一核对。当每条评审意见被单独核查时，PremiseCheck在全部三个领域达到与GPT-5.5相当的准确率，而成本仅为其一半左右；在NLP评审上，成本更是仅为四分之一。
tldr: PremiseCheck通过让LLM在不读论文的情况下将评审意见拆解为显式前提、再用廉价判定模型逐一与论文核对，在保持与前沿LLM相当的核查准确率的同时将成本降低至约一半（NLP领域仅为四分之一）。
en_tdlr: PremiseCheck combines an LLM that rewrites review comments into explicit premises without reading the paper with a cheap decision model that verifies each premise against the paper, achieving accuracy comparable to frontier LLMs at roughly half the cost (a quarter on NLP reviews).
